prompt: Write the body (about 150 words) of an insurer's answer to a personal injury petition in Texas: a general denial and three affirmative defenses that fit a sideswipe while changing lanes. Plain text. Call the parties only 'Plaintiff' and 'Defendant'. No names, placeholders, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1182; do not mention it.)
text:
Defendant, for its answer to Plaintiff's Original Petition, generally denies each and every allegation contained therein and demands strict proof thereof as required by the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure. Pursuant to Rule 92, Defendant further asserts the following affirmative defenses.

First, Plaintiff's own negligence caused or contributed to the collision. Plaintiff failed to keep a proper lookout, failed to confirm that the adjacent lane was clear before moving, and failed to yield the right of way as required when changing lanes. Under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, any recovery must be reduced by the percentage of responsibility attributable to Plaintiff.

Second, the injuries and damages claimed were not proximately caused by the subject collision. Plaintiff's alleged conditions may be attributable to preexisting or unrelated medical conditions, or to subsequent events, and Defendant is not liable for those.

Third, Plaintiff has failed to mitigate damages. Plaintiff did not follow reasonable medical advice or undertake reasonable steps to limit the claimed losses, and any recovery must be barred or reduced accordingly.
